slides.headline: Something is wrong with this mirror. Can you spot it?
slides.sub: Édouard Manet, A Bar at the Folies-Bergère, 1882

slides.headline: Paris, 1882
slides.text: A busy night at the Folies-Bergère. Suzon stands behind the bar, a huge mirror at her back.

slides.headline: She looks at you
slides.text: Tired and far away, she looks straight at you, as if you just ordered a drink.

slides.headline: But in the mirror
slides.text: Her reflection has slipped far to the right. And there, she leans toward a man.

slides.headline: That man is you
slides.text: In the mirror he stands right in front of her. So he must be standing where you are.

slides.headline: A mistake?
slides.text: For a century critics said Manet got it wrong. In 2000 a researcher rebuilt the scene: from one side, it works.

slides.headline: Meanwhile, above the crowd
slides.text: Top left corner: two green feet. A trapeze act is on, and nobody at the bar looks up.

slides.headline: Back on the bar
slides.text: Next to the champagne, bottles with a red triangle: Bass, an English beer, in the heart of Paris.

slides.headline: And one bottle is signed
slides.text: On its label Manet wrote: Manet 1882. A year later he was gone. This was his last great painting.
